description: Weighted dendrogram of average annual spending per dog-owning or cat-owning household, 2025. Pet / editorial cost group / reported category is a hierarchy; branch width encodes dollars with one common linear scale. All reported categories are retained. Species means have separate household denominators and must not be added into a grand total.

usermeta.idiom: Dendrogram (node-link tree, cluster layout): hierarchy of pet → type of cost → category, with leaves aligned and branch width proportional to dollars. Kirk, hierarchical idioms (tree hierarchy / dendrogram).

scales.branchWidth: Common zero-based linear dollar scale, with no minimum-width floor. Small branches remain small; printed labels retain the amounts.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
usermeta.courseBasis: W06 Network and Trees, slide 7, and Network idioms (Kirk), PDF page 2, explicitly allow line width for quantitative attributes in a dendrogram. The root groups the two species for navigation; it is not a summed household budget.
usermeta.readingNote: All reported categories are included. Dog items sum to 2,521 Australian dollars; the published 2,520 Australian dollars total differs by one Australian dollar from rounding. Averages include owners who spent nothing in a category. A source dash is missing, not zero.
usermeta.clickSelection: story-interactions.js pins a main-mark selection in pinnedKey and clears it on an empty-space click. Species hues, quantitative colours, symbol areas and plotted positions retain their meanings.
